scope: Source-only demand-led mobility feature implementation; deployment and runtime qualification are owned by the root task.

tests.type: CPU fixtures and API contract tests; not detector accuracy evidence

api.optimisticRevision: expectedRevision; stale writes return 409; invalid references/config return 422
api.persistence: Independent SQLite config key mobility:<site-id>; config save does not reset cameras, tracks, or native rules.

verified: Existing line events produce camera-local per-class rolling totals.
Continuous observed entry/exit gates produce completed movement travel times; first sighting inside a gate does not fabricate entry.
Source gaps, wall stalls, prediction-only gaps, projection loss and capacity loss cannot become completed movements.
Line-boundary touches preserve the prior side with the existing rule hysteresis.
Stopped-zone blockedSeconds unions confirmed-active fresh intervals; concurrent vehicles do not double the zone duration.
Missing and predicted frames and candidate dwell are excluded from blockedSeconds; new evidence must requalify after loss.
Cleared episodes expire from rolling windows; bounded count-history eviction marks coverage truncated.
Queue/crossing integration preserves historical evidence during wall stalls while marking current measurements unknown.
Deleted or disabled rule references fail closed through configurationIssues.
limits: Measurements use each camera source timestamp; no conversion to Isaac scenario time.
Camera-local identity only; overlapping views are not fused or deduplicated.
Observation coverage is frame receipt coverage, not detector recall or verified physical exposure.
Blocked time is a measured lower bound after confirmation, not full incident age.
Vehicle obstruction uses a ground anchor rather than a validated full vehicle footprint.
Rolling measurements reset on process, configuration or source-session changes.
Queue extent is an estimate from connected observed ground anchors; visibility and unresolved tracks can make it a lower bound or unknown.
Pedestrian wait samples exclude first-seen-inside waits; completion requires an observed far-side exit, not signal-phase knowledge.
CPU validation does not establish real-scene movement/count/queue accuracy.
